title: `test_hmm_from_blosum62` panics in libnail
body: On `dev` at `837ba60`, `cargo test -p libnail` panics in `structs::profile::tests::test_hmm_from_blosum62`. The other 21 libnail tests pass. A plain `cargo test` stops at the failure, so nail's 37 tests run only under `cargo test -p nail`. Nobody has diagnosed it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/95b307ba
notes.text: Diagnosis. The panic is `todo!("fix this")` inside the test itself, at `libnail/src/structs/profile.rs:1373`. No library code fails. Commit `036babf` (2025-07-25, "removed Hmm struct") moved the test from the deleted `hmm.rs`. It swapped `Hmm::from_blosum_62_and_sequence` for `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq`, commented out both assertions and put the `todo!` in their place. The old test checked two things on the `Hmm`. First, `hmm.model.composition` against 20 expected values. `Profile` has no composition field, and nothing computes one from a sequence anymore, so that half has nothing left to check. Second, `hmm.stats.forward_lambda` against 0.703323. `Profile::from_blosum_62_and_seq` computes `fwd_lambda` with the same formula, `LN_2 + 1.44 / total_entropy`, so that half could be pointed at `prf.fwd_lambda`. The old lambda assert had no `.abs()`: `(lambda_correct - lambda) < 1e-4` passes for any lambda above 0.7032, so it never checked an upper bound. Nobody has run the old test at `036babf^` to see whether it passed then.
